session_cue.text: Sir Phidipaldi slapping the Reeve with his glove

previous.text: The party reached Brandonsford at sunset, following a treasure map to places they did not recognize.
Reginald warned of a Clurichen trickster that comes into town from the riverbanks each night.
Eric the Reeve offered a bounty for the dragon. Sir Phidipaldi then slapped him and challenged him to a duel, which Eric did not accept.
Lady Hilda offered to join the party for pay, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would come back for her.
Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for hire, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
Bentley and Gill told the party that supplies have stopped reaching Brandonsford.
Quinn promised Sir Phidipaldi 100 gold to help him get back at Bentley, whom he blames for stolen ale.

current.where_you_are: Sir Phidipaldi is at the bar of the empty Golden Egg Tavern with its owner, Quinn. Wayman Tisdale and Dr. Uriah are across the street in the Clumsy Fox Tavern. Dunk is at Farmer Gill's farm, drinking with Gill on the porch before bedding down in the barn.

Your goals.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley and collect his promised 100 gold.
Find the treasure the party's map leads to.
Kill the black dragon and drag its body into Brandonsford for Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
Get Farmer Gill's prize mule Shamus so Dunk can start his own farm.
Acquire Warwick the smith's mithril chain shirt, which would fit a normal-sized person but not Dunk.

Standing in your way.text: Gill says Warwick always refuses to sell the mithril chain shirt he displays in his shop.

What could help.text: If Sir Phidipaldi makes a show of delivering Quinn's water-filled bottles to the Golden Egg, they can see what happens.
If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will join them to hunt the dragon.
If the party agrees on a fee, Lady Hilda will join the hunt, though she says she cannot kill the dragon herself.
If Dunk helps kill the dragon, Gill might trade Shamus for it, though Gill never agreed to a deal.

Still unanswered.text: What empties Quinn's stock every night?
What happened to the shipments that stopped reaching Brandonsford?
Where did the black dragon come from?

Meanwhile.text: A small black dragon roams outside Brandonsford and took the woodsman George's arm. Gill's three sons are out trying to kill it.

threads.name: The treasure map
threads.note: The party is following a treasure map whose marked locations they do not recognize; the treasure is still unfound.

threads.name: The Clurichen trickster
threads.note: Reginald warned that a trickster called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night up to no good, an open danger and question.

threads.name: The dragon and Eric the Reeve's bounty
threads.note: Eric offered 1000 gold for killing the black dragon and dragging its body into town (beat_18), and the rumours, George's encounter, Gill's sighting and his sons' hunt all bear on this one dragon. Sir Phidipaldi's insult and duel challenge to Eric (beat_20, beat_21) strained relations with the bounty-giver but did not end the offer.

threads.name: Lady Hilda's offer to join the party
threads.note: Lady Hilda said she cannot kill the dragon herself but would join adventurers for money, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would talk to the Reeve and come back for her services; her stated purpose ties her to the dragon hunt.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer of hire
threads.note: The thief Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for 100 gold a week, with a per-kill rebate, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

threads.name: Brandonsford's missing shipment
threads.note: The town's restocking shipment is a week overdue and goods have not reached town in months; nobody has yet gone after it.

threads.name: Farmer Gill's mule Shamus
threads.note: Gill offered Dunk the mule for 100 gold; Dunk asked to trade work, Gill pointed to killing the dragon, and Dunk is sleeping on the offer with no deal settled.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Warwick the increasingly paranoid smith displays a superb mithril chain shirt he refuses to sell, an item the party may want.

threads.name: Quinn's deal against Bentley
threads.note: Quinn's stock vanishes nightly and he blames Bentley; Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help get back at Bentley for 100 gold and to stage a fake ale delivery. The mystery of the vanishing stock bears directly on this deal, so it is one situation.

facts.text: Find the treasure the party's treasure map leads to.
Where are the locations marked on the party's treasure map, and which one holds the treasure?

classification.grounding_justification: The session explicitly states the party does not recognize the map's marked locations and only assumes the treasure lies in one of them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying the places on the map is mostly a matter of locating them, though finding which holds the treasure takes some discovery.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: The answer is mainly instrumental for finding the treasure; nothing suggests a hidden revelation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Locating unknown landmarks in unfamiliar country plausibly supports asking locals and exploring the surrounding land.

facts.text: Reginald the frog warns that a little trickster called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The creature is only said to be up to no good; no specific harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: It is described as a little trickster, suggesting mischief rather than serious harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on the word of a single talking frog, a local witness but unconfirmed.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald describes a nightly recurring pattern of it coming into town.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can heed the warning and avoid where it goes, though its whereabouts are unknown.

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into town each night?

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald's warning explicitly says it is up to no good without saying what, clearly raising the question.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden nightly activity and its intent.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning the trickster's nightly doings could explain local troubles, but nothing yet ties it to them.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could watch the riverbanks at night and follow the creature or ask locals.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
Lady Hilda would join the party for pay to hunt the dragon.

classification.support_basis: A seasoned, armored companion would strengthen the party's fight against the dragon, at an unstated fee.

facts.text: George, a capable woodsman living a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox, encountered the dragon and could be questioned about it; Eric says he might show up at the tavern tonight.

classification.support_basis: As a first-hand witness, George could tell the party where and how he met the dragon, helping them find and face it.

facts.text: Where does the black dragon lair?

classification.grounding_justification: The dragon is only said to be outside town, with George and Gill having seen it; its location is an ordinary gap for the hunt.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Finding the lair is a single discovery.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Witnesses George and Gill, and Gill's sons out hunting, offer leads to follow.

facts.text: Where did this black dragon come from, the first seen near Brandonsford since Sir Brandon's dragon was killed centuries ago?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley and Gill stress nothing like this has happened in hundreds of years, and Gill says he doesn't know where dragons come from.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer could reveal a cause behind the dragon's appearance, possibly tied to the Sir Brandon legend.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could reframe the town's legend and the current danger.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Local lore and witnesses could be pursued.

facts.text: A black dragon, not a large one, roams outside Brandonsford; it took the woodsman George's arm, and Gill's three sons are out trying to kill it.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: It has already maimed one person, so further injury to those who meet it is a clear outcome.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Loss of a limb or death to those who confront it.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George's injury and Gill's sighting are direct testimony.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Gill's sons are actively hunting it, but it ignored Gill and no ongoing attacks on town are established.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could kill the dragon for the bounty.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned-looking noblewoman with chain mail and a shield, offers to join the party for money in hunting the dragon, though she says she cannot kill it herself; no fee has been named.

classification.support_basis: An armored, more experienced companion would strengthen the party against the dragon, though she admits she cannot kill it alone and her price is unknown.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk with Eric the Reeve and come back to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: Sir Phidipaldi only stated the party's intention; nothing shows Lady Hilda relies on their return beyond a general wish for paid work.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a greasy-haired thief, offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill people with the wasp; for allowed kills he would give back 5 gold each if he can do what he wants with the bodies. Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

classification.support_basis: Ned would add a killer and his wasp to the party, but play never tied his hire to any particular want or debt, and he is driven by a wish to kill.

facts.text: What happened to the shipment to restock Bentley's tavern, due a week ago, and why has nothing reached Brandonsford in months?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley states the shipment is a week overdue and hurting the town, and Gill says nothing has come into town in months; the absence is clearly raised by several sources.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the cause behind a months-long interruption of supplies, an underlying hidden circumstance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining why the town has been cut off could change understanding of its troubles, possibly connecting to the rumored dragon, though play has not linked them.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could question townsfolk, follow the supply route and look for the lost shipment, plausibly supporting following leads.

facts.text: Dunk gets Farmer Gill's shabby prize mule Shamus, which Gill offers for 100 gold so Dunk can start his own farm.
When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Gill said the big work needed is killing the dragon outside town; Gill did not settle a deal.
facts.uncertain_reason: Gill named the dragon as the work needed but never explicitly agreed to trade Shamus for it.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon could get Dunk the mule without paying 100 gold, though Gill never confirmed the trade.

facts.text: Acquire Warwick the smith's mithril chain shirt, which Gill calls probably the best in the world; it would fit a normal-sized person but not Dunk.
facts.uncertain_reason: Only Dunk has heard of the shirt, from Gill, and no party member has yet said they want it.

facts.text: Gill says Warwick displays the mithril chain shirt in his shop but always refuses to sell it.
Why is Warwick growing more paranoid and covering his shop with lucky charms and clovers?

classification.grounding_justification: Gill describes Warwick's daily-growing charm collection and paranoia as conspicuous behaviour, offering only his own guess that it is to ward off Ingrid.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause or fear behind Warwick's behaviour, possibly tied to his refusal to sell.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting local colour; it may explain Warwick but is not a major revelation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could question Warwick, Ingrid or townsfolk, a modest line of inquiry.

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for stealing his ale, and collect Quinn's promised 100 gold.

Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi plan to stage a fake ale delivery to the Golden Egg: Quinn brings up bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering them, to see what happens.

classification.support_basis: The staged delivery is bait that could reveal who or what empties Quinn's bar at night, which the party needs before acting against Bentley; whether anything takes the bait is untested.

facts.text: What empties Quinn's stock each night, leaving glasses empty or knocked over by morning?

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn explicitly describes a recurring nightly loss he cannot explain, and only suspects Bentley without proof.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden culprit and their method behind a repeated pattern.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the culprit would confirm or overturn Quinn's accusation against Bentley and change who the party acts against.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: A staged delivery and a night watch on the bar naturally support investigation.
